messages:
Maya Patel: thanks everyone for the great Q&A today. posting the process questions we heard so leadership can answer in one place. please keep replies short so i can fold them into the follow-up doc.

Kaitlin Moore: two quick asks from product: 1) are we consolidating cadence across teams? 2) how strict are perf blocks for runtime/serving changes?

Zoe Kim: summary from leadership: default product cadence = biweekly feature releases. infra/runtime teams should prefer shorter loops (weekly) for minor fixes. teams can opt into weekly canaries when they need fast feedback. we will not force a single cadence org-wide.

Zoe Kim: perf gate update: any PR touching serving/runtime needs a bench link plus a short note describing load profile. block if p95 increases >=8% OR memory per request increases >=10% OR qps drops by >7% compared to baseline. put mitigation plan in PR if block triggers.

Ben Ortiz: oncall follow-up: primary = 1 week, secondary = 2 weeks shadow. new handoff ritual: a single pinned handoff message in #eng-oncall every Monday 08:45 PT with incident summary + runbook link. please include active mitigations in the handoff.

Nora Schultz: SLA question from PMs: what latency guidance do we show for Dedicated and do we do auto-fallback?

Maya Patel: Dedicated customers get contract p95 targets; guidance we'll publish: small-seq p95 <= 180-220ms, mid-context p95 <= 300-400ms, long-context up to ~600ms depending on model. automatic fallback chains (variant -> lighter-quantized variant -> cross-region) are enabled by default for critical routes; customers see an incident note when fallbacks occur.

Kaitlin Moore: can we get a concise PR template snippet to require bench artifacts and a rollback plan so merges don't slip?

Zoe Kim: draft PR checklist (feel free to edit):
```
PR checklist:
- tests: unit + minimal integration
- bench artifacts attached (baseline + candidate) with load profile noted
- perf diffs: latency_p95, qps, memory_per_request (block if p95 >= +8% or memory >= +10% or qps <= -7%)
- deployment plan: canary window, success criteria, rollback steps
- security/data review if touching auth or customer data
```

CI-Guardian: policy: PRs that touch /runtime or /serving will require a perf artifact link; missing artifacts will cause the CI policy check to fail. see https://redwood.example/ci/perf-policies

Ben Ortiz: request for eng-sre: publish canonical metric ids and a tiny bench script so teams can auto-compare in CI.

Nora Schultz: leadership also asked for examples of when to choose weekly canaries vs biweekly release in practice. can we get 3 short scenarios for the follow-up doc?

Maya Patel: yes 1: i'll run a 30-min follow-up office hours tomorrow 4:00pm PT to walk through scenarios, review the PR checklist, and show the handoff template. action items: Zoe to file PR checklist repo patch by EOD, Ben to post bench script in #eng-sre by tomorrow noon, eng-sre to publish metric ids. i'll post notes and an FAQ blurb about SLAs and fallbacks after the office hours. thanks all :thumbsup:
